Title: Compression-spring end treatments change inactive coils, pitch, and solid height
Caption: Textbook end-style conventions from the supplied FE Handbook. End sketches are schematic and enlarged; gold strokes denote ground seating faces, not an added part. Formulas depend on the stated end convention and nominal dimensions; manufacturing tolerances require separate treatment.

Title: Empirical spring-wire strength decreases with increasing wire diameter
Caption: Original plots of the five empirical coefficient pairs tabulated in the supplied FE Handbook. Displayed diameter interval is illustrative; applicable procurement specifications and size ranges must be checked before using this model for actual material acceptance. Curves are not experimental data or current supplier certifications.

Title: A helical torsion spring converts arm force into wire bending and angular deflection
Caption: Assigned coil-body torsion-spring model, negligible arm compliance. Units converted consistently to N·m/rad. Despite its name, a helical torsion spring wire is primarily in bending. Ki=(4C²−C−1)/[4C(C−1)], C10. Load direction, winding, and material limits need consideration in real design.

Title: A spring operating envelope must avoid solid contact and account for cyclic stress
Caption: Same closed-ground spring as1321. Assigned40–100 N cycle stays below an illustrative5 mm solid-contact margin. L0/D is a slenderness descriptor, not a universal buckling threshold; end restraint and guidance matter. Fatigue life is not inferred without material endurance and surface information.

Title: Thin closed cylinders carry twice as much hoop stress as longitudinal stress
Caption: Assigned thin cylindrical shell at internal gauge pressure2 MPa, mean radius100 mm and wall5 mm. Left is the end view of an isolated half-cylinder of axial length L; hoop traction arrows act tangentially at the cut edges. Right shows longitudinal tension. Membrane treatment excludes local openings, supports, and radial-stress detail.

Title: End-cap pressure force is balanced by longitudinal shell tension
Caption: Same closed thin cylinder as1327. Forces are drawn on the isolated end-cap segment: pressure pushes outward and shell tension pulls inward. Mean-radius thin-wall areas are used consistently; exact inner/outer radii would introduce small corrections.

Title: A spherical vessel has equal membrane tension in both surface directions
Caption: Assigned thin spherical shell under uniform internal gauge pressure, remote from openings. The drawing is a hemisphere side view, with pressure resultant acting over projected circular area. Equal biaxial stress is a property of spherical symmetry, not a cylindrical-shell hoop result.

Title: Corrosion allowance reduces the available pressure-resisting wall thickness
Caption: Illustrative end-of-life membrane calculation: nominal thickness less corrosion allowance. Cross-section layers are enlarged for visibility, not scaled. Manufacturing tolerance, measured remaining wall, localized attack, joint efficiency, and applicable code equations are separate requirements; this is not a code thickness determination.

Title: Free pipes expand thermally; fully restrained pipes develop compressive stress
Caption: Assigned uniform heating of a straight elastic steel pipe, stress-free at initial temperature. Free thermal strain isαΔT=.0006. Full restraint imposes mechanical strain−αΔT and compressive stress−EαΔT. Actual support flexibility, temperature gradients, bends, and yielding can change reactions; pressure effects omitted.
